query:
Both Claudette and Vera expressed concern about parking in relation to the no. 22 planning application. Who was specifically concerned about parking being blocked during construction works, and who was opposed to the development on character grounds?

Options:
A. Claudette
B. Femi
C. Jordan
D. Vera
context:
[1] (about=Vera, episodic, t0 @2025-05-05T18:52:00) Already sent mine to the council. Main concerns: scaffolding access, parking disruption during works.
[2] (about=Claudette, episodic, t0 @2025-05-05T11:17:00) I saw it this morning. I remember when no. 22 was a single-storey cottage. This street does not need any more bulk added to it. I shall be objecting.
[3] (about=Claudette, episodic, t4 @2025-05-19T19:34:00) include the driveway at no. 19 in the note. That corner has been bad for months
[4] (about=Claudette, episodic, t2 @2025-05-12T15:28:00) I have mixed feelings. I understand the frustration with commuter parking. But £80 a year is an additional burden on residents who have always parked freely here. I remember when you could park outside your own home without paying for the privilege. I am not convinced.
[5] (about=Jordan, episodic, t8 @2025-06-02T16:40:00) seriously though Claudette, were the old parties this busy?
[6] (about=Femi, episodic, t1 @2025-05-12T15:15:00) Quick question for the street, the council is consulting on a Residents' Parking Zone for our road. Proposal is controlled hours Mon–Fri 8am–6pm, permits at £80/year. Thoughts? I want to know where everyone stands before the meeting.
[7] (about=Claudette, episodic, t8 @2025-06-02T16:19:00) Femi, you have done Len proud. I was quite emotional seeing the whole street out together. This is what Maple Street is for, people, not parking schemes.
[8] (about=Femi, episodic, t0 @2025-05-05T11:04:00) Quick question for the street, has anyone seen the planning notice on no. 22's gate? They're applying for a rear dormer and loft conversion. Consultation closes Friday.
[9] (about=Claudette, episodic, t8 @2025-06-02T16:42:00) busier sometimes. In the 90s people brought out cassette decks and stayed until dusk
[10] (about=Marcus, episodic, t0 @2025-05-05T11:22:00) I'd want to know about the skip and scaffolding access. Last time there was building work that side it blocked the school gate for two weeks.
[11] (about=Claudette, core, t2 @2025-05-12T15:28:00) opposes the £80 annual resident parking permit scheme, sees it as an additional burden on residents who previously parked freely
[12] (about=Claudette, core, t2 @2025-05-12T15:28:00) could accept a trial period for the parking scheme, but not permanence
[13] (about=GROUP, said_by=Claudette, group-interaction, t4 @2025-05-19T08:53:00) the joint note will include the driveway at no. 19, which has been a problem corner for months
[14] (about=Vera, core, t2 @2025-05-12T15:28:00) supports the parking scheme because home visits require parking on clinic days
[15] (about=Vera, core, t0 @2025-05-05T11:04:00) already sent individual objection to council, main concerns are scaffolding access and parking disruption
agent_answer: Vera was concerned about parking being blocked during construction works; Claudette opposed the development on character grounds.
